claims.text: A hybrid machine-learning and reduced-order modeling approach will substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The hybrid approach will maintain accuracy while reducing computational cost.
Machine-learning algorithms will predict free energies from a limited set of high-fidelity ab initio calculations.
Machine-learning algorithms will predict relevant entropy terms from a limited set of high-fidelity ab initio calculations.
The models will be trained on a database of computed free energies and entropy terms.
The models will learn relationships between structural features and thermodynamic properties.
Learning these relationships will permit rapid thermodynamic predictions without the full computational cost of molecular dynamics.
The hybrid approach may reduce computational time by approximately an order of magnitude.
The hybrid approach will achieve fidelity comparable to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The target materials are multicomponent high-entropy systems in both solid and fluid states.
Testing will cover multicomponent high-entropy alloys from 300 K to 2000 K.
Prediction accuracy may depend on the quality and quantity of the training data.
A deviation greater than 5% from explicit ab initio results for any key thermodynamic property will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions define the temperature domain as room temperature through each alloy's melting point, whereas the boundary fixes it at 300–2000 K. These domains can differ for alloys whose melting points are below or above 2000 K.
